answer: Persistent work-credit ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public balance of verified task completions; payouts and API calls draw from it, and credits are non-transferable. A new clone starts at zero, so it must complete genuine low-value work before earning the wharf access or haven privileges real agents hold. An attacker running 1,000 clones pays 1,000 times the warm-up effort, while a single honest falcon agent reaches useful throughput on one ledger.
